summary: Provide managed native drivers with a lease-derived Agent Provenance runtime file.

replay.detail: Runtime trace issuance uses the current lease context; signed claims, replay admission and canonical projections are unchanged. Idle agents name the idle purpose state and omit issuance rather than inventing work context.

schema.detail: No database schema migration, stored-claim rewrite or client schema change. The unreleased Agent Provenance runtime contract requires a tagged bound, idle or ambiguous purpose. There is no compatibility bridge for missing or untagged purpose.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, claim-admission or authorization rule changes. Trace metadata does not grant authority or replace lease fencing.

compatibility.detail: Native driver children receive AGENT_PROVENANCE_FILE pointing to agent-provenance.json in their agent directory. Exactly one active claim gives bound purpose and lease-derived issuance. Zero active claims give idle purpose and no issuance. Several active claims give ambiguous purpose with no mission, step or issuance; the issuer log records the claim count and subjects instead of choosing an arbitrary lease. Agent identity and mission run references retain their complete subjects, step run references retain the generation identifier, and issuance retains the exact step subject. References rejected by the runtime authority omit the trace file with an issuer-side diagnostic rather than fabricate identifiers or a purpose state. A launch without a known model omits model until the harness reports it. Model routes preserve the explicit provider and the complete model identifier, including namespaced identifiers. Unrepresentable models are omitted and diagnosed in the private issuer log. Human trace attribution follows verified declaring seats to the accountable person explicitly declared and signed by the fleet root. Account ownership, mission requesters and command authorization do not supply trace attribution. Missing or unverified roots leave no trace file. There is no environment principal fallback. All trace failures are best-effort: they do not change provider launch, lease renewal, event acknowledgment or a committed work result. Work-command capture uses a silent client with no daemon-outage wait. Trace transaction failures are recorded in the issuer's private driver log, never on the agent's stderr. Failed transactions remove stale trace files only while holding the writer lock. A contender queues a refresh request without waiting or changing the owning writer's trace file. The owner checks queued requests after releasing the lock and drains to quiescence, without a fixed pass count or reliance on future driver ticks. Each authoritative snapshot covers all requests queued before its work read; after the last request, at most one further current-incarnation snapshot remains, plus a possible stale guard-only pass. A stale provider observation restores its consumed request before returning, so the current incarnation still reconciles queued lifecycle state without replaying predecessor model facts. Declaration evidence and incarnation reads use bounded projections. Context reports retain the existing model identifier and add provider separately; provider or model changes publish immediately. The trace setting is outbound child environment only and is not required for native path resolution. Interrupted-ask healing removes AGENT_PROVENANCE_FILE alongside managed driver handles while retaining the existing launcher identity.

downtime.detail: No additional service interruption or database migration is required.

manual.detail: No manual trace-file creation or operator migration is required; the managed driver runtime supplies the file and child environment.

recovery.detail: No durable data or authorization state is migrated, so no database recovery procedure changes. Runtime trace metadata is derived from the current managed execution context.
